Major IT/phone upgrades(17th July to 31st August inc)
Due to major IT infrastructure upgrades and significant building works, our IT servers will be shut down from the afternoon of Friday 17th July.
As the summer holidays begin, Reception will close at 12.30pm on Friday 17th July. From Monday 20th July, our telephone system will be partly closed until Monday 3rd August, with phone calls directed to a single point which will be monitored infrequently. As Reception will remain closed throughout the school summer holidays, voicemail messages will be not be routinely monitored or responded to until it reopens at 8am on Tuesday 1st September for our staff training day.
Our annual Open Evening is on Wednesday 23rd September 2026, 6pm to 8.30pm. (No booking required.)
WE ARE DELIGHTED TO WELCOME YOU TO THE COWPLAIN SCHOOL
We have always been a school that has challenged our students to achieve highly whilst developing them to be confident and respectful young people. At the heart of this is our fantastic curriculum, which promotes three central strands of understanding diversity, thinking hard and developing character, which are at the heart of everything we do. We challenge our students to work hard, enjoy learning and achieve highly, providing a wide range of opportunities for them to succeed, both within and outside the curriculum, whilst supporting them with a highly effective pastoral network.
Our last Ofsted inspection in March 2024 stated that "Pupils value the warm and welcoming atmosphere here. Pupils appreciate the support they get from staff, which helps them learn well. Staff show a genuine care for pupils, who feel safe and happy at this school.", something that we are incredibly proud of and which underlines that The Cowplain School is a happy and vibrant place to learn.
Mr IR Gates, Principal

Special educational needs and disabilities (SEND)
Welcome to the Learning Support Department
At The Cowplain School, our Learning Support Department is committed to ensuring that every student can succeed academically, socially, and personally. Guided by our school motto Work hard. Enjoy learning. Achieve highly. we provide an inclusive environment where all learners are supported to access the curriculum, develop independence, and achieve their full potential.
In line with the SEND Code of Practice (2015), we adopt a person-centred, collaborative approach to identifying and meeting Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We support students across the four broad areas of need: Communication and Interaction, Cognition and Learning, Social, Emotional and Mental Health, and Sensory and/or Physical Needs.
High-quality teaching forms the foundation of our provision. As part of our Ordinarily Available Provision, all students benefit from well-structured lessons, adaptive teaching, personalised strategies, consistent routines, and reasonable adjustments that ensure equitable access to learning. When additional support is needed, we provide targeted interventions, specialist teaching, and carefully planned programmes that reflect each student’s strengths and individual needs.
We are proud to have two Hampshire-designated Resourced Provisions (RPs): one for Specific Learning Difficulties (Dyslexia/SpLD) and one for Communication and Interaction Needs (namely, Autism). These provisions offer enhanced support, specialised environments, and tailored interventions delivered by experienced staff.
Our department works closely with pupils, families, teachers, and external professionals to ensure that provision is effective, evidence-based, and continually reviewed. We are committed to creating a safe, supportive, and aspirational community where every learner feels valued and able to thrive.
If you would like further information or wish to arrange a visit to the school or our Resourced Provisions, please contact our SEN Department at sen@cowplainschool.co.uk or telephone 023 9261 2020 ext 326
Resourced Provision at The Cowplain School
The Cowplain School is proud to offer two Resourced Provisions (RP), providing enhanced support for students with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) whose primary needs are identified as Communication and Interaction Difficulties—Autism and Specific Learning Difficulty (SpLD) -Dyslexia. Placement decisions for both the Autism Unit and the Dyslexia Unit are made by Hampshire County Council SEN, in line with the SEND Code of Practice and local authority criteria.
Our Autism Resourced Provision has been thoughtfully designed to provide structured individual workstations, a calm space for pupils who require time away from the main school environment, and areas where therapeutic interventions can take place as specified within EHCPs. A dedicated sensory area is available, and pupils may choose to spend their break times within the nurture area, or the Resourced Provision, if this best supports their needs.
Students allocated a place in the Dyslexia Resourced Provision receive targeted, specialist support, including two one-to-one or small-group sessions each week with our Specialist Dyslexia Teacher. Additional in-class support is provided by trained Learning Support Assistants to promote access to the curriculum and the development of independent learning strategies.
Across both provisions, teachers and support staff receive enhanced training, and all pupils benefit from personalised Pupil Passports to ensure that their individual needs, strengths, and aspirations are well understood and effectively supported.
If you would like further information or wish to arrange a tour of the school, including a visit to either unit, please contact our SEN Department via sen@cowplainschool.co.uk or by calling 023 9261 2020 ext 326 to book an appointment.

Careers Education and Guidance
The Cowplain School believes all students should have access to the best advice and are well informed when making important choices about their future.
The Careers Leader at The Cowplain School is Mrs E Zambo.
If you wish to make enquiries about careers education, information and guidance please contact at The Cowplain School please contact the Careers Team:
Careers Leader: Mrs E Zambo
e.zambo@cowplainschool.co.uk
Careers Advisors: provided by Hampshire Futures
careers@cowplaincloud.co.uk
The Cowplain School is committed to ensuring our students have access to impartial and inspirational careers information, advice and guidance.
The Cowplain School Careers Programme supports all students from Year 7 to Year 11 and is carefully planned to introduce students to the world of work and careers; promote aspirations by introducing students to a wide range of career and education opportunities and pathways; develop employability skills; provide encounters with employers; and enable students to prepare for and make choices for their future.
Careers education, information, advice and guidance is delivered via careers lessons and across the curriculum, working with a wide range of providers, including Hampshire Futures, and local and higher education providers.

All students will have individual careers guidance interviews with qualified careers advisors and you can also contact them for advice at careers@cowplaincloud.co.uk

We would like to congratulate our 2026 GCSE students on achieving excellent results for The Cowplain School.
In English, 74% of students achieved a Grade 4 or above in either English or English Literature, with almost 70% achieving a Grade 4 in Maths. Over 60% of students achieved Grade 4s in both subjects. Other subjects achieving excellent results included Spanish, in which over 80% of students achieved a Grade 4, and the performing arts, with Music, Drama and Dance all achieving 70%+, as did GCSE Sport.
In total, students at Cowplain achieved a huge number of the highest grades, with 34 x Grade 9s, 37 x Grade 8s and 93 x Grade 7s.
Standout results for individual students included WH, with 9 x Grade 9s and 1 x Grade 8, and OB, 7 x Grade 9s, 1 x Grade 7, 1 x Grade 6, with many other students achieving incredible results.
There were many more students who achieved outstanding GCSE results, who we will report on soon, so huge congratulations to the class of 2026 on their success in achieving those exceptional results.

Pastoral structure
We understand that your child’s wellbeing is extremely important to you, and it is a priority for us. Here, at The Cowplain School, we have an excellent Pastoral Team which will look after your child’s wellbeing for the duration of their time at the school.
We have a unique set up whereby our five Heads of Year do not teach, and are therefore on hand all day, every day, to work with their specific year group. We also have five Assistant Heads of Year who works alongside the Heads of Year.
In addition to this, we also have outstanding care with regards to your child’s mental health. Miss Graham is our onsite School Psychologist/Mental Health Lead, who works with our students who need additional support.

Should you be worried about your child’s well-being or behaviour at school, we would encourage you to contact your child’s Head of Year in the first instance, either by telephoning Reception, or emailing the Head of Year. Heads of Year will always try to respond as quickly as possible, but we recommend making an appointment to see or speak to them. Email addresses can be found above.
Resilience Centre
For those students who are not educated in the main school for all their lessons, we have our Resilience Centre. Students accessing their education here benefit from high adult to student ratios and bespoke individualised timetables. These students receive a broad and balanced curriculum offer. Pastoral and welfare care for these students is provided by Ms L Alden (RC Leader), Mrs P Stainsby (HLTA), Mrs P MacCallum (HLTA), Ms J Rankin (Behaviour Intervention Worker) and Mrs D Creighton (Behaviour Intervention Worker). The Resilience Centre is line managed by Mr J Peters (Assistant Headteacher).

Partner primary schools
We work very closely with our Partner Primary Schools, Our staff visit local primary schools on a regular basis to work with younger pupils and staff on English, Maths and Language skills. We also invite pupils from Years 4 to 6 to visit Cowplain and take part in PE activities and dance and technology workshops. Working closely with our Partner Primaries enables a smooth transition to secondary school.
We support local primary schools with a Business project where we teach Year 6 pupils about running a business, including marketing, advertising and how to prepare effective presentations.
We also support primary schools with their productions by sending Year 11 GCSE Dance and Drama students to help choreograph and direct their performances. We have volunteer students from our Backstage Club who teach pupils about sound and lighting techniques.
In the summer term Year 5 and 6 pupils are invited to The Cowplain School to work with pupils from different schools to solve problems, experience what life is like at Cowplain and get to know members of staff.
Towards the end of the summer term our staff visit each Partner Primary School, along with some of our Year 7 Student Ambassadors, to speak with the Year 6 pupils about the transition to The Cowplain School. They have the opportunity to ask questions and complete a CV about themselves which we pass to their new Tutor and the Pastoral Team.Pupils who choose The Cowplain School from outside of the local area are invited to visit and meet our staff; pupils have a tour of the school and spend time with other Year 6 pupils.
Our SENCO and our Learning Support Key Teachers meet with the SENCO of the primary schools in the summer term to gather information about pupils who will be transferring to us with Special Educational Needs.
We have no catchment area. Students currently join The Cowplain School from the following schools, and further afield:

Hart Plain Junior School
Horndean Junior School
Mill Hill Primary School

Purbrook Junior School
Queen’s Inclosure Primary School
Woodcroft Primary School
To arrange a visit to the school, please contact Reception on 023 9261 2020 or email office@cowplainschool.co.uk.

Assessment and Reporting
Assessment and Reporting 2025-26
At The Cowplain School we have regular, rigorous assessments for all year groups twice a year; all assessment results are published in students' reports and can be found on Insight. Examples of reports are given on links below. The reports will also contain information on attendance which is not given in every report example.
Every report for every student in every year group contains the following:
1) The assessment results in the form of a percentage and the average assessment result of all the students who have completed the assessment.
2) The students’ pathway, which gives students a target grade range to not limit students to one specific target grade.
In the guided pathway students are aiming for a grade 5. The scaffolded students are aiming for a 5 to 7 grade range and the independent students are aiming for a 7 to 9 grade range. The terms guided, scaffolded and independent describe the type of learning we would expect the student to do, e.g. scaffolded students receive more support by the teacher scaffolding the learning for them, while independent students are expected to work more independently.
3) An attitude to learning and an attitude to home learning grade (ATL and ATH grade criteria can be found in Resources).
4) An indication whether the student is currently exceeding (E), meeting (M) or a concern (C) in relation to their target pathway.
5) A rank order position for each subject and the average KS2 rank order (based on English and Maths) on entry for comparison. This rank order information will be used to change class sets after the reporting.
All assessments for all year groups, except for practical assessments, take place in classroom or the hall. Students have an assessment Assembly or assessment Reflection Time two weeks before the assessments start, followed by two weeks of revision in class. Home learning is based around revision too.
Students from Year 7 to Y10 are issued with a Knowledge Organiser, a booklet which summarises all the knowledge to learn to be prepared for the assessment. In Year 11 we expect students to purchase revision guides, which can be obtained via this link
Year 11:
The 1st Assessment Cycle is based on students having regular extended learning checks to facilitate frequent exam practice followed by detailed feedback on how to improve. These extended learning check points take place regularly in all subjects (except for Art and Photography). This extended assessment period is used to in inform the first set of students’ reports. The students’ reports will be published in the week of 17th November, followed by an online Year 11 parents evening on Thursday 20th November.
The 2nd Assessment Cycle takes place over a period of three weeks, starting from the 7th January to 23rd January. This assessment period is designed to mimic the real GCSE assessment period as much as possible. These reports are published in the week of the 23rd February and are followed by an in-person parents evening (on Thursday 26th February). There will also be an opportunity to collect the results early on Thursday 12th February as part of a Mock Exam Result day, which will take place in the afternoon. Students will be invited to collect results in-person and parents will be welcome too.

The 1st Assessment Cycle takes place from the 24th November for one week, followed by the students’ reports, published in the week of 5th of January and an online parents evening on Thursday 15th January.
The 2nd Assessment Cycle takes place from the 17th June for approximately ten days. These assessments will take place in the hall. They are followed by students’ reports published in the week of the 13th July.

The 1st Assessment Cycle takes place from the 12th January for one week, followed by the students’ report, published in the week of the 9th February and an in-person parents evening on Thursday 12th February.
The 2nd Assessment Cycle takes place from the 1st June for one week, followed by the students’ reports, in the week beginning 22nd June.

The 1st Assessment Cycle takes place from the 3rd November for one week, followed by the students’ report, published in the week of the 24th November. The online parents evening will take place on Thursday 12th March, to discuss options and upcoming assessments.
The 2nd Assessment Cycle takes place from the 20th April, followed by the students’ reports, published in the week of the 11th May.

Reading
We believe that developing a strong reading culture and supporting our students to become confident readers are essential to their future success. Reading is an integral part of our school day and our students have a daily, timetabled twenty-minute reading session each day.
Throughout their time at The Cowplain School, our students are taken on a carefully researched and planned reading journey (click here for Reading Curriculum Map). Each year, our students read a minimum of three books in Reading Time. The texts have been carefully chosen to support our three curriculum strands: “Thinking Hard, Developing Character and Understanding Diversity” and consist of modern classics, which tackle challenging, thought-provoking themes. Tutors read aloud to students to ensure that they have good reading role models with regards to prosody. Students follow along with the book and complete a comprehension, vocabulary, and inference quiz fortnightly on a Friday.
We have a strong team of Reading Leaders who champion reading across the school and provide targeted support to younger learners whom they read with on a one-to-one basis four times a week in the library.
We encourage our students to use decoding skills when encountering new, complex words and implement a synthetic phonics programme for Y7 in J, K and L groups and Y8 students in K and L using the Butterfly phonics and the Abigail Steel training programme.
Our enthusiastic readers can take part in the 16 before 16 challenge that encourages them to read sixteen classics and modern classics that have played an important role in shaping modern literature.
Half-termly reading DO NOWs are now embedded in every subject area with students reading a wide range of subject-specific articles.
